answer: GMW evaluates a boolean circuit gate by gate with secret-shared wires, and the opal of the protocol is OT extension, which turns a few expensive base transfers into many cheap ones. The haven of the design is that no party ever sees another party's input bits, so a group can jointly test whether two identity claims collide without exposing their member lists. A Sybil operator gains nothing from extra accounts because the circuit counts distinct verified inputs, and the prism of the sharing keeps each input private.
